citation.authors: Imai S, Kajiyama S, Kitta K, Miyawaki T, Matsumoto S, Ozasa N, Kajiyama S, Hashimoto Y, Fukui M
citation.title: Eating Vegetables First Regardless of Eating Speed Has a Significant Reducing Effect on Postprandial Blood Glucose and Insulin in Young Healthy Women: Randomized Controlled Cross-Over Study

population.description: 18 young, healthy Japanese women (Kyoto Women's University volunteers) who completed all three days of 21 registered; free of metabolic disease, eating disorders and relevant medication, no family history of T2DM; not screened by a glucose tolerance test; age and BMI as printed, mean ± SD.

protocols.name: slow_carb_first
protocols.description: Slow eating (20 min) with carbohydrate first: rice 0-6 min, fish 6-13 min, vegetables 13-20 min. Breakfast of Table 1 (671 kcal; total 105.4 g carbohydrate, 24.5 g protein, 16.3 g fat) at 09:00 after a 12 h overnight fast (arrival 08:30); blood at 0, 30, 60, 120 min, minute 0 = 09:00, when the paper says the meal was consumed and the IAUC baseline was taken ('baseline concentration at 9:00'); the samples, 'at 0, 30, 60, and 120 min after test meal consumption', are read as counted from 09:00. Each food is entered as one meal at the minute its stated eating segment began (the paper's segments last several minutes; the model takes a bolus): rice = Table 1 row 'Boiled while rice' (74.2 g carbohydrate, 3 g dietary fiber, 5 g P, 0.6 g F); fish = row 'Frozen box of fried fish' (21.1 g carbohydrate, 0 g fiber, 15.9 g P, 5.2 g F); vegetables = tomato + broccoli + sesame oil rows added (carbohydrate 7.1+3+0 = 10.1 g, fiber 1.5+2.6+0 = 4.1 g, P 1.1+2.5+0 = 3.6 g, F 0.2+0.3+10 = 10.5 g). Table 1 prints Carbohydrate and Dietary Fiber as separate columns and its carbohydrate is total (the printed 63% of 671 kcal is 105.4 g x 4), so carbs_g = carbohydrate minus fiber: rice 74.2-3 = 71.2 g, fish 21.1-0 = 21.1 g, vegetables 10.1-4.1 = 6.0 g (98.3 g in all); fibre_g is the printed fiber. Foods as the Methods name them (rice, fried fish from a frozen bento, tomato and broccoli with sesame oil), eaten with 200 g of water; segment start minutes are sums of the stated segment lengths.

meals.food: tomato and broccoli with sesame oil

protocols.description: Fasting plasma glucose of the 18 analysed women (Results, characteristics); the paper does not say on which morning or at what clock time it was drawn (study mornings were after a 12 h overnight fast, sampled at 09:00); a 30-minute fasted run-in stands for the single sample.

findings.description: Plasma glucose at 30 and 60 min, slow eating with carbohydrate first, mean ± SEM

location.quote: postprandial blood glucose at 30 min (slow eating with carb. first vs. fast eating with veg. first; 7.09 ± 0.34 vs. 5.94 ± 0.24 mmol/L, p < 0.05. vs. slow eating with veg. first; 5.53 ± 0.25 mmol/L, p < 0.01, mean ± SEM) and 60 min (slow eating with carb. first vs. fast eating with veg. first; 5.88 ± 0.34 vs. 4.95 ± 0.18 mmol/L, vs. slow eating with veg. first; 4.97 ± 0.16 mmol/L, both p < 0.05)
